cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put 'butler' above your answer on the murder-mystery board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We both said butler at the same time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Simultaneous guesses aren't deductions. List your evidence; I'll put it in order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The muddy shoes. Same evidence you used.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put 'muddy shoes' under my answer. Evidence goes with the conclusion it supports. Yours can stay below.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 ranks A's answer above B. A3 corrects B2 simultaneous guesses into supposedly deficient reasoning; A5 appropriates B4's shared clue under A's top conclusion, using methodological authority to control the contest.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 equal answer prompts A3 evidence request. B4 equal clue removes substantive superiority, so A5 changes the written arrangement without inventing an existing difference in reasoning.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 reasonably insist on equal deduction. A's refusal of equality affects a real shared game rather than a bare status slogan.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's parity to put the clue physically under A's answer, exposing how far the claimed expert will go to remain first.

specificity.evidence: A1 murder-mystery board and butler answer, B4 muddy shoes, and A5 explicit writing instruction supply all needed board facts.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 gives one concrete placement instruction with a corrective rationale and retained ranking; no new unseen writing is claimed.
